material.text: subagent-live-status-plugin: Shows the model used by currently running subagents in the OpenCode TUI

# subagent-live-status-plugin [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/rjdev-git/subagent-live-status-plugin.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/rjdev-git/subagent-live-status-plugin/blob/main/LICENSE) Live model status for running subagents in the OpenCode TUI (terminal UI). This plugin shows which model each active subagent is using, so you can see what is running without opening each session individually. It matters when subagents use models different from your main agent: the panel shows each subagent's model, so you can confirm it matches its configuration. Current version: `1.4.6` The project was renamed from `opencode-subagent-model` to `subagent-live-status-plugin`; the plugin id, storage namespace, and command ids move with it, so the persisted compact toggle resets once. ## Live preview ## Why use it - The whole subagent team is visible all the time: working roles in colour, idle roles in grey - Working instances nest under their role like subfolders, each with its own model and speed bar - Browse all active subagents from one searchable picker - Open any subagent session directly from the UI - Keep the status compact when you want less visual noise ## Example output A tree of agent roles. A role shows the agent definition; every running instance nests under it with its session title, model (only when it differs from the role's model), and speed bar: ```text Project Team Members 1/5 1.explore [built-in] ├ Inspect… Go/Grok 4.7 ▓▓▓▓░ └ Audit r… ▓░░░░ 2.reviewer Go/Kimi K3.1 3.qa Go/Kimi K3.1 4.writer Claude/Sonnet 4.5 5.research Go/Kimi K3.1 ``` `explore` is a built-in agent working a task in a repo that also has `.opencode/agents` definitions: its role row shows the fixed `[built-in]` tag instead of a model. Its `Inspect…` instance run uses the resolved session model. States: - Grey row = role waiting (idle); idle and working roles carry the same text and differ by colour only - Coloured role = at least one instance of that agent is working; the colour comes from the agent definition (`color`), falling back to the theme's success green - `├` / `└` rows = running instances, one per session, scoped to the tab you are viewing - A failed or interrupted instance keeps its row in warning colour for 30 seconds, then folds back into its role row The title counts roles currently working over roles known. The body caps at 10 lines; anything beyond folds into: ```text +2 more · /subagents ``` Role rows are numbered (` 1.`, `20.` reserved), instance rows are unnumbered. Both row shapes fill exactly `width` cells. Only instance rows carry the speed boxes, so they align vertically with each other. Row width is measured at runtime from your terminal itself, no config needed. In priority order: (1) the renderer's own layout tree knows the sidebar container's width in cells (authoritative), (2) terminal pixel width and cell metrics estimate the width, and (3) the plugin uses the configured fallback width. The model label clips when the row is too tight: the provider keeps at most half of the budget, and the model name takes the rest. On an instance row one separator cell sits between the model field and the boxes; the boxes are tight against each other, and role rows have neither. **How to read the boxes.** The boxes show an instance's measured output speed; each filled box is a step up in real speed, not a proportional fraction. | boxes | model is producing | | --- | --- | | ▓ | 5–19.9 tokens/sec | | ▓▓ | 20–49.9 | | ▓▓▓ | 50–69.9 | | ▓▓▓▓ | 70–100 | | ▓▓▓▓▓ | above 100 (strictly) | | ░░░░░ | below 5 (or speed still unknown) | Compact mode keeps the old summary: ```text sub 3 ``` ## Features - Live team tree in the session UI (`sidebar.content` by default) - Role rows with configured model, instance rows with live model and speed - Built-in agents working in a repo with agent definitions get a temporary `[built-in]` role row (no model) while their session runs - Instance model shows only when it differs from the role's model - `/subagents` command and `/subagent-models` alias - Palette command: `Show running subagent models` - Palette command: `Toggle compact subagent status` - Type-to-filter picker for agent, model, title, and elapsed time - Direct open action for each subagent session ## How it works Which agents the panel shows is decided once per session as a snapshot: with at least one agent definition in `.opencode/agents` (charter mode) it lists only those definitions (skipping agents marked `hidden: true` or `primary`), and built-in agents appear only as temporary rows while one of their sessions runs in this tab. Without definitions, it falls back to all discovered agents except `hidden: true` and `primary`. Mid-session changes to `.opencode/agents` take effect on the next session, not the running one. A session becomes an instance row when it is a child session currently marked `running`, and it belongs to the tab the viewer is in. A session that ended with `outcome: failed` or `interrupted` stays visible in warning colour for 30 seconds, then folds back into its role row; when the role existed only as a temporary built-in row for that session, the row disappears with it. The title counts how many roles have a working instance. It resolves the instance model in this order: 1. the session model 2. the subagent's configured agent model 3. the nearest parent session model 4. `unknown model` So an instance may resolve a model different from its role's `agent.md`: a per-session override wins. The panel shows the instance's model label only when it carries information: when the resolved model differs from the role's model, or when the instance's model is unknown. The displayed label follows the format `ProviderName/ModelName`, and appends ` (variant)` when relevant. If a label is missing, the plugin falls back to the provider or model ID. The sidebar rows use the short form: the provider's last word (`OpenCode Go` → `Go`) and no variant. The speed bar is computed from the instance's own assistant messages: output tokens divided by the time they streamed, so it reports tokens per second. The five boxes fill in bands: 1 box at 5–19.9 tokens/sec, 2 at 20–49.9, 3 at 50–69.9, 4 at 70–100, and 5 above 100 (100.0 exactly stays in the four-box band). Below 5, all boxes are empty, as they are while the speed is still unknown. The plugin syncs each running subagent session (session and messages) into the TUI data layer when the session appears on the panel or when its execution starts, then re-syncs the session's messages as new assistant output arrives. ## Commands ### `/subagents` Opens a searchable list of running subagents. It includes: - agent name - resolved model - session title - elapsed time - session ID The title line is `agent · model`, where the agent clips at 24 cells and the model at 96 cells, each independently cell-aware. Type to filter the list. Press Enter to open the selected session, or use `alt+o` to open it without closing the picker. Example: ```text /subagents explore ``` ### Palette commands - `Show running subagent models` - `Toggle compact subagent status` ## Configuration Add the plugin in `opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc` if you prefer JSON with comments): ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "subagent-live-status-plugin", "options": { "placement": "sidebar.content", "bind": "ctrl+shift+s", "compact": false, "width": 35 } } ] } ``` ### Options | Option | Type | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `placement` | `"sidebar.content"` \| `"sidebar.footer"` \| `"prompt.footer"` | `"sidebar.content"` | Where the live status is rendered | | `bind` | `string` | unset | Keybind for the subagent picker | | `compact` | `boolean` | unset | Forces compact mode (`sub N`) | | `width` | `number` | `35` | Cell budget for a sidebar row; also the cap when width detection succeeds, and the fallback everywhere detection is unavailable | | `cellPx` | `number` | `8` | Pixels-per-cell assumption for the last measurement rung only (when the terminal reports no pixel resolution); runtime measurement handles modern terminals | The `debug` option ships as a diagnostic aid for future investigations: `debug: true` enables it and appends a JSONL record per recompute to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/subagent-model-debug.jsonl`, or to `~/.local/state/opencode/subagent-model-debug.jsonl` when `XDG_STATE_HOME` is unset or empty; a string value overrides that path. The directory is created `0700` and the file `0600`, and the dump stops after 2000 records per run. It is off unless enabled, is not part of the requirements contract, and is planned for removal once it goes unused. ## Installation ### Install from npm (one config line) Use this unless you want to modify the plugin. Add the plugin to `opencode.json` (or `opencode.jsonc`) with one config line: no clone, no build, no `node_modules`: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "subagent-live-status-plugin", "options": { "placement": "sidebar.content", "bind": "ctrl+shift+s", "compact": false, "width": 35 } } ] } ``` OpenCode fetches the package itself. When a newer version appears on npm, `/reload` picks it up. ### Install from source Use this when you want to modify the plugin, run its tests, or cannot fetch from npm. Otherwise skip it. ```sh git clone https://github.com/rjdev-git/subagent-live-status-plugin.git cd subagent-live-status-plugin npm install mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/plugins ln -s "$PWD" ~/.config/opencode/plugins/subagent-live-status-plugin ``` ### Update (source install only) npm installs do not update this way; they pick up the newly published version on `/reload`. ```sh git pull npm install # only when package-lock.json changed ``` After installing or updating, reload the TUI with `/reload` or restart OpenCode. ### Alternative installs The plugin is discovered from the OpenCode plugin directories. Global config path: ```text ~/.config/opencode/plugins/subagent-live-status-plugin/ ``` Project-local path: ```text /.opencode/plugins/subagent-live-status-plugin/ ``` You can also symlink the plugin directory into place: ```sh ln -s /path/to/subagent-live-status-plugin ~/.config/opencode/plugins/subagent-live-status-plugin ``` Copy the directory instead of symlinking also works; updates then need a re-copy. ## Development ```sh npm install npm run typecheck npm test ``` ## Repository layout ```text package.json package metadata and exports src/index.ts plugin bootstrap entry src/tui.tsx TUI commands, slots, and dialogs src/lib/collect.ts model resolution, role tree, and layout logic src/lib/collect.test.ts unit tests for the data layer docs/superpowers/specs/ design documents ``` ## License MIT
